videos?limit=100&depth=1&sort=createdAt.title: How much can I borrow? A first-time buyer’s guide
videos?limit=100&depth=1&sort=createdAt.caption: The five checks lenders make, with a real-life example…

captions.alt: How much can I borrow? A first-time buyer’s guide: captions

videos?limit=100&depth=1&sort=createdAt.transcript: Hey there, I’m John Nugent, and welcome to LifeMap. I’m going to answer the question I get asked more than any other… how much can I actually borrow? Don’t worry, we’ll keep it simple. And we’ll follow a real-life example, so you can see exactly how it works. Let’s meet Aoife and Conor. They’re renting at the moment, paying €1,500 a month… and they’re dreaming of their own front door. Between them, they earn €85,000 a year. So… how much could they borrow? Lenders look at five things. Let’s take them one by one. First… loan to income. As a rule, you can borrow up to four times your combined income. For Aoife and Conor, that’s €85,000 times four… which is €340,000. Some lenders can stretch a little further for high earners. But you’d need to be approved at four times first. Second… your deposit. Every lender asks for at least ten percent of the house price. So we add that to Aoife and Conor’s €340,000. And that gives us a house price of €377,778. That’s €340,000 to borrow, plus a deposit of about €37,778. That’s ten percent of the price. Now, here’s some good news. There’s a Help to Buy scheme that can go towards your deposit. It’s for first-time buyers of a new home priced under €500,000… and you’ll need to have paid income tax and DIRT in Ireland over the last four years. You can claim the lowest of three things: ten percent of the property value, the tax you’ve paid over those four years, or €30,000. Whichever comes out smallest. Third… net disposable income. That’s simply whether you’d have enough left over to live on each month. Lenders work this out with a formula based on your family size, not your actual spending. Fourth… your debt servicing ratio. Lenders limit how much of your income can go on repaying debts, like loans or credit cards. If you’ve already got a lot of borrowing, adding a mortgage could push you over that limit. The good news? Aoife and Conor only have one small loan, so neither of these is a worry for them. Fifth… repayment capacity. Lenders need to be sure you can comfortably afford the monthly payment. Over thirty-five years, a mortgage of €340,000 comes to roughly €1,350 to €1,450 a month, depending on the lender. Some lenders also offer cashback, usually one to two percent when you draw down. That can make the monthly payment a touch higher… but you get some money back at the start. Now… Aoife and Conor are paying €1,500 a month in rent, and they’re saving €300 a month on top. That’s €1,800 a month they’ve shown they can manage. And that comfortably covers the repayment. They could even look at a shorter mortgage term than thirty-five years. So there you have it. Five checks, and a clear picture of what Aoife and Conor could borrow. Your own numbers will be different… and that’s completely okay. That’s what we’re here for. Pop your details into LifeMap, and we’ll talk you through your own options. Book your expert appointment today with us.
